question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2r-1}+1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2r-1}+1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{r}^{2}}{\sqrt{2r-1}-1} & = \\ \frac{4{r}^{2}}{\sqrt{2r-1}-1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2r-1}+1}{\sqrt{2r-1}+1} & = \\ \frac{4{r}^{2}(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)}{(\sqrt{2r-1}-1)(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)} & = \\ \frac{4{r}^{2}(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)}{(\sqrt{2r-1})^{2}-{1}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{4{r}^{2}(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)}{2r-1-1} & = \\ \frac{4{r}^{2}(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)}{2r-2} & = \\ \frac{2{r}^{2}(\sqrt{2r-1}+1)}{r-1} & \end{aligned}
$$
